Loading methods are stubs whatever the receiver. A JDK method that takes a loader is blocked by the router, because it would ask the loader for classes from inside host code. new URLClassLoader(...) is a stub that returns a loader which only remembers its URLs; <init> stays listed so a sample's own subclass can still extend the real class.

Providers are tables of class names that the JDK loads and constructs, shared by the whole JVM. Every route to one (Security.getProvider, getProviders, and getProvider on each engine class) is a stub returning a private copy, dev.javabyte.env.SimProvider. These lines cover a real provider that might still slip through: reading it is harmless, changing it or subclassing it is not.
